tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)

prep.what: Build the persistent, priority-aware Postgres job queue that the Sweeper (t21) runs on — with lease/heartbeat/reclaim semantics so jobs survive daemon crashes without double-running.
prep.understand: Lease = a job is atomically claimed by one worker for a time window. Heartbeat = worker pings to extend the lease. Reclaim = expired leases re-enter the queue. Cap = max concurrent jobs of a given kind. The governor (429 pause) from the triage agent era should hook in here for rate-limiting. This is the foundation everything in Phase 6 sits on — get the schema right and t21, t22, and t29 all become straightforward to wire.
approach: Design and apply the `jobs` Postgres migration via `db/migrate.ts`: `id (uuid)`, `kind (text)`, `payload (jsonb)`, `priority (int)`, `status (queued|running|done|failed)`, `lease_expires_at (timestamptz)`, `heartbeat_at (timestamptz)`, `retry_count (int)`, `max_retries (int)`, `window_id (text nullable)`, `created_at`.

Implement `JobQueue` class: `enqueue(kind, payload, priority, cap)` with cap enforcement, `dequeue(kinds[])` using `UPDATE...WHERE status='queued'...RETURNING` with `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` for safe concurrency, `heartbeat(id)`, `complete(id)`, `fail(id, reason)`, `reclaim()` to reset expired running→queued.
Add governor hook: check a rate-limit signal before `enqueue`; if hit, defer rather than error.
Write unit tests: enqueue+dequeue round-trip, concurrent dequeue returns exactly one winner per job, heartbeat extends lease, expired lease reclaimed on next dequeue, cap blocks over-limit enqueue.
resources: `lib/pg-board-repository.ts` and `lib/writer.ts` — Postgres patterns in this codebase
`db/migrate.ts` — migration runner to add the new schema
PostgreSQL `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` docs for atomic job claiming
Triage agent source — governor/rate-limit pause pattern to reuse
Bun test runner + existing 1400+ test suite (run after each step for regressions)

tasks.title: Daemon-side cross-process refresh lock (prereq for live SWEEPER_REPOS)
tasks.notes: The refresh CLI takes a per-repo O_EXCL single-flight lockfile. Before flipping the sweeper on against live SWEEPER_REPOS, the daemon must honor the SAME per-repo lock across a job's whole lifecycle. Until done: run refresh ONLY while the sweeper is stopped.

prep.what: Make the sweeper daemon acquire and respect the same per-repo file lock that the CLI refresh tool uses — so the two processes can't race to corrupt a repo's working tree.
prep.understand: The CLI uses `O_EXCL` (exclusive create) on `SWEEPER_STATE_DIR/<repo-slug>.lock`. The daemon has only an in-process lock — different processes can't see it. The fix: daemon acquires this same file lock at job-start, holds it through the full `refreshRepo` call, and releases it in a `try/finally` on complete/fail/crash. The `RefreshRunners` seam is already injected, so the lock wraps the call site in the daemon's job handler, not inside `refreshRepo` itself.
approach: Read the CLI refresh code to confirm the exact lockfile path formula (`SWEEPER_STATE_DIR/<slug>.lock` or similar).
In the daemon's job handler (where `refreshRepo` is called): acquire `fs.open(lockPath, 'wx')` before the call, wrap in `try/finally` to close+unlink on any outcome.
Handle lock-already-held gracefully: check mtime to distinguish stale vs live lock; if live, defer the job back to the queue with a short delay rather than failing it.
Add a cross-process test: write the lockfile manually, assert the daemon defers; delete it, assert the daemon runs the job.
resources: CLI refresh source — O_EXCL lockfile logic and path formula
`lib/sweeper/` daemon job handler — the call site to wrap
Node.js `fs.open(path, 'wx')` for O_EXCL-equivalent exclusive create
`SWEEPER_STATE_DIR` env var and directory layout
t28 notes (go-live hardening advisor log) for context on the marker/lock design
